I've been working this land for 40 years. I know what it needs. My back isn't what it was, and two of my grandchildren are in the city now, so I hire machine services for the heavy work. But I still manage everything myself.

This land does wheat in winter, maize in summer — all 5 mu, same fields, same rotation I've done my whole life. That doesn't change.

**Wheat:** I'll buy the improved variety the seed shop in town carries — probably Jimai 22 or whatever the county station has been pushing. Not the expensive hybrid stuff, just the reliable improved seed. I'll put down compound fertilizer at sowing and topdress with urea when the wheat is jointing. I've always used roughly one bag of compound and half a bag of urea — that's about 15 kg nitrogen per mu total. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide sprays — one herbicide early, one for rust and aphids in spring. I'll hire the rotary tiller.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant maize. I use hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 has been good to me for years, I'm not switching. I apply fertilizer in two shots: compound at planting, urea at the big bell stage. Maize in summer usually gets rain, but I'll irrigate once or twice if it turns dry. I'll spray once for pests — corn borer mostly. No-till, straight into the wheat stubble with the seeder service.

My yields aren't the county record but they're steady. That's what matters at my age.
